name: Gbiri-Niragu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Aderibigbe, Adeyinka Gloria 2010. Verb phrase of Kahugu language (99pp thesis; Glottolog MED phonology_or_text) — not found online

sources.citation: Roger Blench website, East Kainji materials index (EKOP.htm) and Gbiri folder, Wayback captures 2015-04-20, 2024-07-24, 2025-05-28.
sources.note: Index lists 'Gbiri — Unpublished' with no link; the Gbiri folder is empty. No Gbiri/Niragu wordlist or phonology is published on the site (the live site is behind a captcha; only /files/ paths serve).
Location, speaker number (25,000, 2000), noun-class prefixes, duodecimal numerals; no phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45–67. DOI 10.15460/auue.2021.93.1.210 (open access, Hamburg University Press).
sources.note: Table of languages (p.48): 'Western — Gbiri — Vigorous — Wenger (2016)'; 'Niragu — Vigorous — Wenger (2016)'; acknowledgement p.47 'Thanks to Rachelle Wenger for information on Gbiri'; Table 12 'arm, hand': Gbiri ka-kyara pl. na-, Niragu ka-tʃara (BCCW 'Kahu'). Phonology/tone discussion is of eBoze only; no statement on Gbiri-Niragu stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In John R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 1), 59–106. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Gbiri-Niragu appears only in the East Kainji tree (Figure 7) and in the sources table ('East — Gbiri — Wenger'). No phonological description of the language; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004 (ms). The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research. Paper for the Hamburg meeting (Gerhardt retirement), 2 Oct 2004. 12 pp.
sources.note: Section 3.1 'Phonology' and 'Tones' describe eBoze (four level tones plus glides) and tiMap; Gbiri and Niragu are named only in the history (Meek 1931 wordlists), Appendix 1 list and Appendix 3 ('arm, hand': Gbiri *u-kula, Niragu ka-tSara). Nothing on Gbiri-Niragu stress or tone.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page gbir1241 (classification Kainji > Central Kainji > Basa-Eastern Kainji > Eastern Kainji > Jos > Kauru; refs: Aderibigbe 2010; Meek 1931 'wordlist or less').
sources.note: Only two references in Glottolog; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wenger, Rachelle (SIL Nigeria). 2016. Unpublished survey / wordlist data on Gbiri and Niragu (cited as 'Wenger (2016)' in Blench 2020: 48 and as data source 'Gbiri — Wenger' in Blench 2018).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only modern first-hand data on Gbiri-Niragu; an SIL survey or wordlist would carry tone marking and possibly a prosodic note. Not located (sil.org blocked; no OLAC record reachable).

sources.citation: Aderibigbe, Adeyinka Gloria. 2010. Verb phrase of Kahugu language. MA thesis, University of Ilorin. 99 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only descriptive work on the language in Glottolog (hhtype specific_feature); a 99-page Ilorin MA thesis normally opens with a phonology chapter that would state tone and, if anything, stress. A scan exists in Hammarström's bibliography (bestfn africa/) but no online copy was found; Ilorin's DSpace search is non-functional.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1982. Ten more wordlists with analyses from the northern Jos group of Plateau languages. Afrika und Übersee 65(1): 97–134 (and 1979, Five wordlists..., A&Ü 62(4): 253–271).

sources.note: Tone-marked East Kainji ('northern Jos group') wordlists with analyses; it is not confirmed from any page opened that Gure/Kahugu are among the fifteen lists, so low priority. A&Ü vols 62/65 are not on the Hamburg OJS (digitised run starts at vol. 93).

sources.citation: Williamson, Kay & Kiyoshi Shimizu. 1968. Benue-Congo Comparative Wordlist, Vol. 1; Williamson, Kay. 1972. Vol. 2. Ibadan: West African Linguistic Society. Columns 'Gure' and 'Kahu'.
